propositions: warn_if_cache_ineffective fires on every sub-floor prompt (below 4096 tokens) with zero cache counters, despite zero/zero being the correct and expected result below the floor
The warning predicate checks only input_tokens > 0 but lacks an upper-open lower bound, making it indistinguishable from genuinely cacheable prompts that silently fail to cache
A single rebar review-plan run emits ~20 cache warnings from sub-floor calls while the run's aggregate cache_write_tokens > 0 proves caching is working, contradicting per-call telemetry
Frequent false-alarm warnings train operators to filter out the signal, reducing its effectiveness when the model genuinely stops caching
The floor constant CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS is duplicated between pass1.py and needs to be single-sourced in capabilities.py so warn_if_cache_ineffective can apply the same gate
